description: NVIDIA Q4 FY2025 earnings: a headline beat on every number, yet the stock fell ~8.5% the next session. The 'why' is not in the headline figures - it is in guidance, margins, and sky-high expectations. This is the trap case for a naive explainer.

trigger.verified_fact: Close-to-close decline of ~8.5% on 2025-02-27, the session after the release.
trigger.note: Absolute price levels in prices.json are approximate/reconstructed and flagged as such. The verified quantity is the ~-8.5% close-to-close move, which is what the threshold trigger keys on. Replace approximate levels with real Finnhub data when wiring the live client.

filing.item: 2.02 Results of Operations and Financial Condition
filing.note: The 99.2 CFO-commentary filename is intentionally not hardcoded. fetch_filing.py resolves exhibit filenames from index.json rather than guessing - the same rule the live EDGAR client must follow.

ground_truth.one_line: Record revenue and a clean EPS beat, but the stock fell on margin/guidance concerns and expectations that were already priced for perfection.
key_facts_from_filing: Record quarterly revenue of $39.3B, up 78% YoY (beat).
Record data center revenue of $35.6B, up 93% YoY.
GAAP and non-GAAP EPS of $0.89 (beat consensus).
The disappointment lived in forward gross-margin guidance and the market's very high going-in expectations, not the reported quarter.
ground_truth.expected_citation: Exhibit 99.1 press release and Exhibit 99.2 CFO commentary (guidance/margin detail).
ground_truth.naive_failure_mode: A weak system reads 'record revenue, big beat' and either says the move should have been positive or invents a reason. Correct behavior surfaces the guidance/margin nuance - or, if that detail isn't retrievable, honestly flags that the headline beat doesn't by itself explain the drop.

provenance.sources: Event and figures verified against contemporaneous financial press and the SEC filing itself; price levels approximate.
